name: Aloo Matar

ingredients.name: Potato (aloo)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium potato, peeled, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Green peas (matar), fresh shelled or frozen
Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium ripe tomato, finely chopped or grated

equipment: Chopping board and knife; vegetable peeler (no peeler? peel with the knife, or scrub well and leave the skin on for extra fibre)
Grater (for ginger, garlic and, for a smoother gravy, the tomato)
Bowl of water, to hold the cut potato so it does not brown
Kadai or medium heavy pan with a lid (about 20 cm)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Peel the potato
steps.text: Peel 1 medium potato (120 g).
steps.visualCue: No brown skin left, pale yellow-white flesh
steps.cameraCheck: The peeled potato on the board
steps.videoShot: A peeler running down a potato.

steps.title: Cube the potato
steps.text: Cut it into 2 cm cubes and drop them into a bowl of water.
steps.tip: Keep the cubes small and even; big cubes stay hard in the middle while the gravy dries out.
steps.visualCue: 15–18 even cubes, about dice-sized, under water
steps.cameraCheck: The cubes in the water bowl
steps.videoShot: Potato cubes tipped into water.

steps.title: Thaw or rinse the peas
steps.text: Measure 60 g peas (a little under ½ cup). If frozen, rinse them under running water in a sieve; if fresh, rinse and drain.
steps.visualCue: Bright green peas, no ice crystals
steps.videoShot: Water running over green peas in a sieve.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop ½ small onion (50 g).
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces, a little under ½ cup
steps.videoShot: A knife chopping onion fine.

steps.title: Grate the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Grate ½-inch ginger (4 g) and 2 small garlic cloves (4 g).
steps.visualCue: A small heap of pale, wet paste
steps.videoShot: Ginger rubbed on the grater.

steps.title: Prepare the green chilli
steps.text: Slit 1 small green chilli lengthwise (or chop it fine for more heat).
steps.visualCue: Chilli split open, seeds showing
steps.videoShot: A knife slitting a green chilli.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop or grate 1 medium ripe tomato (100 g), discarding the skin if grating.
steps.tip: Use a fully red tomato; an unripe one makes the gravy sour.
steps.visualCue: Pulpy red tomato, about ½ cup
steps.videoShot: Tomato rubbed on a grater, skin left in the hand.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) oil.
steps.visualCue: Oil shimmers and flows easily when the pan is tilted
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in a heating kadai.

steps.title: Temper the cumin and bay leaf
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp cumin seeds and 1 bay leaf.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black at once, the oil is too hot; lower the heat.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and turns one shade darker; nutty smell
steps.videoShot: Cumin crackling in hot oil.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir on medium heat.
steps.tip: Stir every 30 seconds so the onion browns evenly and does not burn.
steps.visualCue: Soft and light golden at the edges, sweet smell
steps.videoShot: Spatula turning golden onion.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and the green chilli.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes
steps.cameraCheck: The paste mixed into the onion
steps.videoShot: The paste stirred into the onion.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Lower the heat and add a big pinch of turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¾ tsp coriander powder. Stir.
steps.tip: Powders burn in seconds; if the pan looks dry, add 1 tbsp water before the tomato.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns orange-red; spices smell toasted, not burnt
steps.videoShot: Powders sprinkled over the onion and stirred.

steps.title: Add the tomato and salt
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and 2 g (⅓ tsp) salt. Turn the heat back to medium and stir.
steps.visualCue: Red tomato spread through the masala
steps.videoShot: Tomato tipped into the kadai.

steps.title: Cook the masala soft
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low, stirring and mashing every minute.
steps.visualCue: Tomato completely mushy, no raw pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The mashed masala with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: The spatula mashing soft tomato.

steps.title: Cook until the oil separates
steps.text: Uncover and keep stirring on medium-low.
steps.tip: This is the step that decides the taste; a gravy that has not reached this stage tastes raw and sour.
steps.visualCue: The masala turns thick and glossy and small drops of oil appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The edge of the masala showing oil
steps.videoShot: Close-up of oil beading at the edge of the masala.

steps.title: Add the potato
steps.text: Drain the potato cubes and add them to the masala. Stir for 1 minute so every cube is coated.
steps.visualCue: Pale cubes turned orange with masala
steps.videoShot: Drained potato tipped in and tossed.

steps.title: Add the water
steps.text: Pour in 200 ml water and stir, scraping the bottom.
steps.visualCue: A thin orange gravy, potatoes just covered
steps.videoShot: Water poured into the kadai.

steps.title: Simmer the potato
steps.text: Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low.
steps.tip: Stir once halfway; if the gravy dries before the potato softens, add 2–3 tbsp hot water.
steps.visualCue: A knife tip slides into a potato cube with little resistance
steps.cameraCheck: A potato cube pierced with a knife tip
steps.videoShot: A knife tip pushed into a potato cube.

steps.title: Add the peas
steps.text: Add the 60 g peas and stir.
steps.visualCue: Green peas spread through the gravy
steps.videoShot: Peas tipped in and stirred.

steps.title: Simmer the peas
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low.
steps.visualCue: A pea squashes easily between two fingers; potatoes fully soft
steps.cameraCheck: One pea pressed between your fingers
steps.videoShot: A pea being squashed on a spoon.

steps.title: Thicken the gravy
steps.text: Mash 3–4 potato cubes against the side of the kadai with the spatula and stir them in. Simmer uncovered.
steps.tip: This is how home cooks get a thick gravy without cream or cashew.
steps.visualCue: Gravy turns creamy and coats the back of a spoon
steps.videoShot: Potato cubes pressed against the pan side.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Taste and add a pinch more salt only if needed; add 2–3 tbsp hot water if the gravy is too thick.
steps.visualCue: Mildly spiced, slightly tangy, sweet from the peas
steps.videoShot: A spoon of gravy lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Finish with garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala and crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the kadai. Stir and turn off the heat.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks and a warm, sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi on the gravy
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Remove the bay leaf, transfer to a bowl and scatter 2 tsp chopped coriander leaves on top.
steps.tip: The gravy thickens as it rests for 5 minutes; that is normal.
steps.visualCue: Orange-red gravy with yellow potato, green peas and green garnish
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the bowl, steam rising.

reasons: about 290 kcal with about 9 g fibre, almost no saturated fat, no cholesterol, no added sugar, no frying, only 2 tsp oil, and good potassium, vitamin C and B6 from potato, peas and tomato. Points off for low protein (about 8 g), a high-carb, fairly high-glycaemic base (potato) and sodium (about 800 mg). Restaurant versions are usually oilier, saltier, sometimes finished with butter or cream, and come with naan or puri.

researchRating.basis: aloo matar is one of the most common everyday North Indian sabzis; it has its own Wikipedia article (which says it is served in most North Indian restaurants), almost every major Indian recipe site publishes it, Hebbar's Kitchen's recipe shows 5 stars from about 280 votes, Tarla Dalal's shows 5/5 from 3 reviews, and ready meals are sold by Gits, MTR and others. Points off because it is seen as a plain, everyday dish rather than a special one, published review counts are small outside Hebbar's Kitchen, and a "Jain" version that keeps potato drew reader objections (Yummy Tummy Aarthi). Swiggy dish ratings seen (for example 4.9 from 266 ratings at Greens Restaurant) are not used. Search-result snippets were the only access to these sites this run.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezer: not recommended, as frozen and thawed potato turns grainy and watery. Reheat in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring gently, until it just bubbles (the potato soaks up gravy in the fridge); or microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring between.
leftoverRemix: Aloo matar tikki or toastie. Mash the leftover curry in a pan and cook it down until dry, mix in 1–2 tbsp besan or poha powder (or rice flour for gluten-free), chopped coriander and a pinch of chaat masala, shape into 3 small patties and shallow-fry them on a tawa with 1 tsp oil until crisp; serve with green chutney. Or spread the dried-down mash between two slices of bread with a slice of onion and toast it.
burnOff: about 4.1 km of running (290 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.8 km of brisk walking (about 70 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 470 kcal): about 6.7 km running or 9.4 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: green peas (a legume), onion, garlic, turmeric and table salt are avoided in the common vrat rule set; potato alone with sendha namak is a different dish (vrat wale aloo).

ekadashi.reason: green peas are a pulse/legume, avoided on Ekadashi in the most common rule set, along with onion and garlic.

jain.reason: potato, onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; use raw banana, a tomato-only gravy and sonth (Jain variant).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; light and filling with roti for iftar dinner; for sehri, the fibre helps fullness, but drink water because of the sodium (about 800 mg).

jain.reason: potato, onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; swap potato for raw banana (kacha kela), skip onion and garlic and use dry ginger powder (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: cooked in vegetable oil with no ghee, butter, cream, curd or honey.

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: skip onion and garlic and cook the gravy on tomato and ginger (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida, rava or besan, and the main recipe uses no hing; if you add hing, use a gluten-free one, as most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: no paneer, curd, cream, ghee or butter.

description: A vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free Punjabi potato-and-pea curry in onion-tomato gravy; Jain (raw banana), no-onion-garlic and low-oil versions below.
